summary: The case reads a blessed Book of the Dead beside a visible hostile elf zombie. C spell.c:learn() calls deadbook(), whose blessed non-invocation branch runs deadbook_pacify_undead() for visible undead; the callback sets the zombie peaceful and makes it flee because its alignment differs from the neutral hero. JS study_book() installs learn(), but js/spell.js:learn() currently skips the effect at its explicit note_unported("spell.c deadbook") branch. The first saved screen difference is the missing C --More-- marker after “You begin to recite the runes.” at step 45; at step 46 C advances the occupation into the Book of the Dead effect while JS follows a different input boundary. Port the whole learn() Book-of-the-Dead arm and the deadbook()/deadbook_pacify_undead() family, then preserve the message wait and monster state changes through the existing caller chain.

source.branch: After read.c:doread() selects SPE_BOOK_OF_THE_DEAD, spell.c:study_book() installs learn() as the occupation. Once the study delay reaches zero, learn() reaches its Book-of-the-Dead arm. In this recording the book is blessed, the hero is not on the invocation position, and a visible hostile elf zombie is adjacent; deadbook() takes the blessed branch and the callback makes the zombie peaceful, then sends it fleeing because its alignment sign differs from the neutral hero.
callers: nethack-c/upstream/src/cmd.c:1816-1817 maps r to read.c:doread(); js/cmd.js:5107 dispatches doread through runReadCommand() at 3379.
nethack-c/upstream/src/read.c:609 calls spell.c:study_book(); js/read.js:803 calls js/spell.js:study_book().

nethack-c/upstream/src/spell.c:639 installs learn() with set_occupation(); nethack-c/upstream/src/allmain.c:485-509 invokes go.occupation(). JS study_book() installs learn(), and js/allmain.js:1595-1624 invokes the saved occupation.

nethack-c/upstream/src/spell.c:385-386 calls deadbook(book) from learn() when booktype is SPE_BOOK_OF_THE_DEAD; js/spell.js:353-355 is the matching branch and currently records note_unported("spell.c deadbook") before returning.
dependencies: deadbook() iterates monsters through iter_mons(deadbook_pacify_undead); the blessed arm needs the source behavior of is_undead(), is_vampshifter(), cansee(), sgn(), mdistu(), tamedog(), and monflee(). Preserve the mpeaceful and mtame updates together with the visible-monster and distance/alignment conditions.

Port all deadbook() arms, not only the recorded blessed branch: invocation checks and object state use invocation_pos(), On_stairs(), inventory iteration, object known/blessed/cursed state, u.uhave, moves/age, mkinvokearea(), d(), and record_achievement(); the cursed arm calls makemon(), set_malign(), unturn_dead(), and mkundead(). Audit existing JS implementations and record/skip any remaining unported callees under the source rules.

evidence: challenges/evaluations/20260926122253-v7.json, evaluated at commit f7e48bd93d6827c557c9a40a255a55cbc5fc8fcf, reports 45/86 matching screens and 41 remaining. Its first mismatch is segment 0 step 45 on key n: C has a dash at row 0, column 30 and cursor [38,0,1], while JS has a space and cursor [5,13,1]. The C recording screen at challenges/cases/v7/blessed-book-undead.session.json step 45 reads “You begin to recite the runes.--More--”. At step 46, after space, C displays “You turn the pages of the Book of the Dead...” and records exercise(attrib.c:509); the evaluation records the first RNG difference at that step (C rn2(19)=17 versus JS rn2(5)=0).

The C recording’s step 43 debug command creates a hostile zombie, yielding an elf zombie next to the hero. Step 44 starts read and shows “[ijkln or ?*]”; step 45 selects n. The C step 48 screen says “The elf zombie turns to flee.” after the blessed Book of the Dead effect.

Upstream spell.c:211-227 defines deadbook_pacify_undead(): visible undead or vampire shifters become peaceful; aligned nearby monsters are tamed or have their tame value raised, and other eligible monsters flee. spell.c:231-331 defines deadbook(); its non-invocation cursed, blessed, and uncursed arms are source behavior, with the blessed arm calling iter_mons(deadbook_pacify_undead) at line 325. spell.c:356-386 calls deadbook() after exercise(A_WIS) when the occupied book is SPE_BOOK_OF_THE_DEAD.

The complete execution path is cmd.c:1816-1817 -> read.c:doread() -> read.c:609 study_book() -> spell.c:639 set_occupation(learn) -> allmain.c:485-509 occupation callback -> spell.c:385-386 deadbook(). JS has the corresponding cmd.js -> read.js:doread() -> spell.js:study_book() -> allmain.js occupation path; js/spell.js:353-355 still skips deadbook() through note_unported(). The callback is reached from production wiring, so tests of deadbook() alone cannot establish this path.
